verses.sanskrit:
शौनक उवाच।
              जनमेजयस्य के पुत्राः पठ्यन्ते लोमहर्षणे। कस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठितो वंशः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम्॥१॥
verses.english: "In the past, the descendant of bharata dynasty, namely king janamjaya, also made a similar request to the right-minded desciple of vyAsa, namely vaishampAyana... and I will recount that from the origin of वृरिश्णि dynasty, basing on whatever vaishampAyana has said to janamjaya... and, on listening the legend of his forefathers in its entirety, that highly perceptive descendant of bharata dynasty, namely janamjaya, has enquired with vaishampAyana... as below...

verses.sanskrit: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे। त्वत्तः कथयतः सर्वे वेद्म्यहं तव परिस्फुटम्॥२॥
verses.english: "Oh, king, there emanated महत्-तत्त्व - the primary principle - from him, later from that principle there came अहम्कार - the I-ness; from this I-ness the five subtle elements like the elements of solidity, liquidity, air, heat and space have come. From them their physical manifestations like earth, water, fire, air, and space have come from them, together with four kinds of living beings - जरायुज, womb-born, अण्डज, egg-born, स्वेदज, moisture-born and उद्भिज्ज, soil-born... this is the age-old process of creation that is going on and on...

verses.sanskrit:
सौतिरुवाच।
              परीक्षितस्य काश्यायां द्वौ पुत्रौ सम्बभूवतुः। चन्द्रापीडश्च नृपतिः सूर्यापीडश्च मोक्षवित्॥३॥
verses.english: And he who copies this harivamsha procedurally, he readily attains the feet of shrIhari, like a honeybee that plunges in on a lotus with an avidity for nectar.

verses.sanskrit: चन्द्रापीडस्य पुत्राणां शतमुत्तमधन्विनाम्। जनमेजय इत्येवं क्षात्रं भुवि परिश्रुतम्॥४॥
verses.english: Glory to sage vyAsa, the son of parAshara, whose birth delighted the heart of his mother satyavat... for the world drinks poetic nectar glided from the lotus called his mouth...

verses.sanskrit: तेषां श्रेष्ठस्तु राजाऽऽसीत्पुरे वारणसाह्वये। सत्यकर्णो महाबाहुर्यज्वा विपुलदक्षिणः॥५॥
verses.english: And the fruit that accrues after listening the pious legend of mahAbhArata tantamount to the donation of a hundred cows with gold-sheathed horns to a scholarly vaidik brAhamaNa.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यकर्णस्य दायादः श्वेतकर्णः प्रतापवान्। अपुत्रः स तु धर्मात्मा प्रविवेश तपोवनम्॥६॥
तस्माद्वनगताद्गर्भं यादवी प्रत्यपद्यत। सुचारोर्दुहिता सुभ्रूर्मानिनी भ्रातृमालिनी॥७॥
verses.english: Submersed in water that seed of the creativity of पर-ब्रह्म has become an egg glowing with golden hue... and the self-created, four-faced-creator brahma, has by himself emerged from that golden egg, गोल्देन् सोउर्cए, whereby we hear of him as स्वयम्भू - the self-reified...

verses.sanskrit: स तु जन्मनि गर्भस्य श्वेतकर्णः प्रजेश्वरः। अन्वगच्छद्गतं पूवैर्महाप्रस्थानमच्युतम्॥८॥
verses.english: If someone copies and donates this harivamsha to a scholarly brahamaNa, to him the fruit of action will be equaling to the fruit of action that accrues on performing a hundred ashwa-medha rituals, four hundred thousand ordinary Vedic rituals, and that accrues on performing raja-sUya or vAjapeya rituals, and that which accrues on donating elephants and chariots. It is of endless merit. So said the sages like vAlmiki and vyAsa.

verses.sanskrit: सा दृष्ट्वा सम्प्रयातं तं मानिनी पृष्ठतोऽन्वियात्। पथि सा सुषुवे सुभ्रूर्वने राजीवलोचनम्॥९॥
verses.english: And he who copies this harivamsha procedurally, he readily attains the feet of shrIhari, like a honeybee that plunges in on a lotus with an avidity for nectar.

verses.sanskrit: कुमारं तं परित्यज्य भर्तारं चान्वगच्छत। पतिव्रता महाभागा द्रौपदीव पुरा पतीन्॥१०॥
verses.english: Hail कृष्ण-द्वैपायन who is said to be the sixth one starting from the great-great-grandfather, i.e., the efficient cause, namely nArAyaNa; hail him who has unlessened opulence of scriptural knowledge; who took birth with an astral shade of nArAyaNa himself; who is the only son of sage parAshara, and who is a treasure trove of Veda-s... hail such a great sage kR^iShNa-dwaipAyana...

verses.sanskrit: स तु राजकुमारोऽसौ गिरिकुञ्जे रुरोद ह। छायार्थं तस्य मेघास्तु प्रादुरासन्समन्ततः॥११॥
verses.english: Sanskrit poets are at liberty to use words at any place in the foots according to exigencies of their metric rules. So, the order of words used by the poet are to be segregated first - called पद-विभाग; then they are to be parsed - called अन्वय, and then प्रति-पद-अर्थ - word to word meaning is drawn, and then तात्पर्य, gist of the verse, is to be presented. Here we are confined to the deriving gist - तात्पर्यम् alone. So far, the division of words in compounds समासा-s is shown in a separate section as above, as an example. It is an impossibility to show the word-separation recursively for all verses in separate paragraphs considering the bulk of this work. Hence, the words are separated in the verse itself, for fear of repetitive work, even if it gives a low-brow reading to purists. Words in smaller compounds - samAsa-s - like तथैव, एवमुक्तस्तु, किम्cइत् etc., will not be cleaved, because this much is to be known to read further. But where compounds have important, or beautiful expressions, they will be cleaved. Further, verse-by-verse meanings cannot be drawn, because the meaning rolls into next foots. Then it is inevitable to push and pull the feet of verses, up or down, to give a meaningful paragraph. Some of our readers are a little confused about this arrangement. Hence we request the readers to go by the verse numbers in such places, and there will be many such pulls and pushes of foots as we go along. If interested to see the verses in original format, text files of verses alone - मूल मात्र श्लोका-s - are given elsewhere on these web pages which the readers may please see.

verses.sanskrit: श्रविष्ठायाश्च पुत्रौ द्वौ पिप्पलादश्च कौशिकः। दृष्ट्वा कृपान्वितौ गृह्य तं प्रक्षालयतां जलैः॥१२॥
निघृष्टौ तस्य तौ पार्श्वौ शिलायां रुधिरप्लुतौ। अजश्यामौ तु पार्श्वौ तावुभावपि समाहितौ। तथैव तु समारूढौ अजपार्श्वस्ततोऽभवत्॥१३॥
ततोऽजपार्श्व इति तौ चक्राते तस्य नाम ह। स तु वेमकशालायां द्विजाभ्यामभिवर्धितः॥१४॥
verses.english: In नैमिशारण्य forest, kulapati and a highly knowledgeable scholar in all scriptures, shaunaka, on venerating him who is the Prime Person आद्य पुरुSअ; supreme ruler ईश; first one to receive oblations in Vedic rituals पुरु हूत; one to whom first orisons are sung पुरु ष्टुत; Eternal Truth सत्य स्वरूप, ऋत; symbolized by mono-syllabled - एक अक्षर - ॐ; प्रणव मय, अविनाशि; Creator ब्रह्म, परमात्म; manifest yet un-manifest व्यक्त-अव्यक्त स्वरूप; primordial सनातन; apparent effect असत्, कार्य-रूप; cause as well as effect सत् आसत्: who is the aggregate of universe विश्वम्, and who is beyond cause and effect सत् असत् परम्: the creator of cause and effect परावराणां स्रष्ट; primordial पुराण; highly sublime परम उत्कृष्ट; immutable अव्ययम्: who brings forth bliss मङ्गल्यं: whose form itself is bliss मङ्गलं; omnipresent व्यापकत्वात् विष्णु, व्यापन शीलम् - सर्व व्यापी; estimable by all the seekers of salvation वरेण्यम्: devoid of sins आगन्तुक दोष शून्यम् - अनघ; pure being सुचि, स्वभाव शुचि; and the one who impels sensory organs इन्द्रियाणाम् प्रवर्तक, हृषीकेश: architect of all sessile and mobile beings cअर अcअर गुरु - and who is Truth, Consciousness, & Bliss सत्-cइत्-आनन्द स्वरूपि, namely to श्रीहरि, that great sage of high rectitude, shaunaka, has enquired with the son of lomaharShaNa-sUta, namely ugrashrava, as below....
verses.bhavadeepa: अजः छगः तद्वत् श्यामौ समारूढौ तथैव कृष्णरूपवन्तौ वेदवृद्धिं प्राप्तौ॥१३॥

verses.sanskrit: वेमकस्य तु भार्या तमुद्वहत्पुत्रकारणात्। वेमक्याः स तु पुत्रोऽभूद्ब्राह्मणौ सचिवौ च तौ॥१५॥
verses.english: "Oh, sUta, you have narrated a marvelous legend mahAbhArata that depicts the legends of all the descendants of bharata dynasty... which in turn is interconnected with the legends of other kings, gods, dAnava-s, gandharva-s, uraga-s, rAkshasa-s, daitya-s, siddha-s and guhyaka-s.... likewise, you also have narrated the incredible deeds of sages and great saints; intrepid exploits of brave and valiant champions; determination of rectitude by the knowers of probity; and other amazing stories which include the incomparable birth episodes of more elevated souls like droNa and bhIShma... oh, sauti, listening to these legends that are ancient and pious from your melodious tone, and that are pleasant to ears and delightful to heart is giving a satisfaction of devouring no less than ambrosia... but, oh, lomaharShana, while narrating mahAbhArata, you have detailed about the succession of kuru dynasty, but the legends of genealogy of वृश्णि and अन्धक remain undetailed... hence, it will be apt of you to give an account of the legends connected with births and actions of them all...
verses.bhavadeepa: वेमको नाम स्वर्गस्थः कश्चिदृषिः तस्य शालायां गृहे द्विजाभ्यां कौशिकपिप्पलादाभ्याम्॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च युगपत्तुल्यजीविनः। स एष पौरवो वंशः पाण्डवानां प्रतिष्ठितः॥१६॥
श्लोकोऽपि चात्र गीतोऽयं नाहुषेण ययातिना। जरासङ्क्रमणे पूर्वं भृशं प्रीतेन धीमता॥१७॥
verses.english: Therefore, he who knows about the earliest creation, he obtains his desired objects, longevity, glory, richness, and family-life, as he desires... At the outset the One without attributes - निर्गुण स्वरूप - also called शुद्ध-ब्रह्म, or शुद्ध-चैत्न्य willed to become many - तत् ऐक्शथ... बहुस्याम् प्रजायेयेति... and started to create. At this time of volition he gradually transfigured himself in प्रकृति and पुरुष by adopting the nature of त्रि-गुण-स्, सत्त्व, रज, and तमस्. In this alloyed state he is called शबल ब्रह्म, or माया-अवcछिन्न-चैतन्यम्. This condition occurs to him as a result of defilement by माय, where माय is the causal factor of diverse creation, and where प्रकृति is महत्-आदिविकारा-s. Because this is ज्ञान विरोधि, contrapositive to gnosis, it is called अ-विद्य, nascence. In such a state of शबल ब्रह्म, ओर् माया-अवcछिन्न-चैतन्यम्, i.e., in the stage of volition, the triad of गुण-s will be in equilibrium. Among the three गुण-s, सत्त्व causes ज्ञान, सुख, plus an inclination to take delight in them. Thus, that सत्त्व became the compose of विष्णु. The guNa rajas causes राग and तृष्ण, where राग, अनुराग is hanker, while तृष्ण is thirsting, which usually, or predominantly occur in male and female relation. So, this guNa rajas is creating सन्गमम्, concupiscence. And the गुण तमस् causes विपरीत ज्ञान, निद्र, आलस्य etc. Hence, it has become causal to लय, involution, thus became the manifestation of रुद्र. When Ishvra left off that stage of volition and about to create, the equilibrium of these three गुण-s gets disturbed. That is the stage of महत्-तत्त्व with three facets, सात्त्विक, राजस, तामसिक. In this stage he is called सूत्र-ब्रह्म, or अन्तःकरण-अवcछिन्न चैतन्यम्. In this form he creates whole universe with names and forms - नाम रूप-आत्मक-सकल-प्रपन्च सृष्टि. At this stage, because there will be an affinity between the creator and the created, स्रष्ठृ-Sऋज्य तादात्म्य स्वरूपम्, that ब्रह्मन् is called विराट्. Then विष्णु will be in the form of ज्ञान-मात्र-तादात्म्य-स्वरूपम्. The cइत्-स्वरूप ज्ञान in the stage विराट् रूप sthiti is called वृत्ति-अवcछिन्न-चैतन्य. And the चैतन्यम् devoid of ज्ञान, liable to become many, is called विषय-अवcछिन्न-चैतन्यम्. As to how the universe came forth from such a brahman who is in the state of विराट्, is as below: 1. तमो सृष्टि: तमस्, मोह, महा-मोह, तमिस्र, अन्ध-तमिस्र - from these there arose static, sessile. 2. तिर्यक्- सृष्टि: पशु-पक्श्यादि सृष्टि - birds and animals. 3. देव- सृष्टि: those who are always सात्त्विक, well satisfied beings. 4. अर्वाक्- सृष्टि: humans who are तम-उद्रेकी-s, दुःख-बहुल- having many tribulations - and who are कर्म-शीला-s - indulgent in works. 5. अनुग्रह- सृष्टि: a creation with a mixture of सात्त्विक-तामसिक गुण-s - animal creation. 6. कौमार- सृष्टि: is of two kinds - प्राकृत and वैकृत - creation of sanatkumAra et al. These six, coupled with three more like 1. महत्- सृष्टि, 2. पन्च-तन्मात्र- सृष्टि; 3. पन्च-भूत-इन्द्रिय- सृष्टि will become the नव-विध- सृष्टि. Thus, this is the first chapter of first canto called harivamsha-parva, in harivamsha-purANa, the sequel of mahAbhArata, narrating the first creation process.

verses.sanskrit: आचन्द्रार्कग्रहा भूमिर्भवेदपि न संशयः। अपौरवा न तु मही भविष्यति कदाचन॥१८॥
verses.english: When besought like this in an obeisant manner, then the noble and virtuous sage vaishampAyana started to narrate that legend, sequentially and descriptively.
